traits.note: FNA vol. 28, Homalothecium (Ignatov; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants in loose to dense tufts or mats, green to rich golden; stems creeping, pinnate; stem leaves erect-appressed when dry, lanceolate, strongly plicate; seta red-brown; capsule inclined to erect, red-brown, cylindric. Typical values are H. sericeum, the silky wall moss (same volume): light green to golden or brownish yellow; stems to 5 cm, branches 5-7 mm, curved and secund from the surface; stem leaves 1.8-2.4 x 0.6-0.8 mm, branch leaves 1-2 x 0.2-0.5 mm, appressed dry, spreading moist; seta 1-2 cm; capsule erect, cylindric, 2-3 mm; on rock and rock faces.

traits.substrates.note: FNA gives rock and rock faces for North America, where it is rare; in Europe H. sericeum is one of the commonest mosses of old walls, limestone and the bark of trees (general bryological knowledge; to cite from Atherton et al., Mosses and Liverworts of Britain and Ireland, 2010).

traits.substrate_reaction.note: Base-rich rock, mortar and limestone, as in European floras; see the note on substrates.

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: Estimate as for other pleurocarp mats; to check against Glime, Bryophyte Ecology.
